title: Precision alert tuning and autonomous runbook orchestrator for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: Our current paging surface emits high-volume, low-actionable alerts during transient regional degradations and backend surges. On-call teams expend time manually deduplicating noise and executing identical mitigations across regions. This ticket designs and implements a 'Precision Alert Tuning' layer plus an 'Autonomous Runbook Orchestrator' that together reduce noisy pages, prioritize genuine SLO-threatening incidents, and automatically execute safe remediation steps (circuit trip, regional load-shed, cache priming) with human-in-the-loop escalation when required. Scope: 1) alert signal scoring + causal fingerprinting to dedupe correlated alarms across services and regions; 2) dynamic thresholds tied to error-budget burn rate and regional capacity headroom; 3) staged automated mitigations (non-destructive -> conservative -> aggressive) executed by the runbook orchestrator; 4) PagerDuty/Slack integration with contextual summaries, rollback playbooks and audit logging; 5) automated canary of runbook actions in a sandbox region before global application. Out of scope: rewrites of metric instrumentation or major telemetry schema changes (handled in ENG-724000).
acceptance_criteria: Alert volume from production regions decreases by >= 60% for noise classes during transient CPU/queue spikes while SLO violation alert fidelity increases (precision) by >= 20% as measured over a 14-day rolling window.
Runbook orchestrator can execute the three-stage remediation flow (throttle, regional weight shift, circuit trip) safely in our sandbox and in production with a human confirmation gate for stage 3.

Automatic dedupe groups are attached to caused-by fingerprints and a single actionable page is created with a synthesized remediation recommendation and links to top-3 affected traces and slowest spans.
All automated actions are audit-logged in the Console and a rollback action is registered for each changeable mitigation with one-click reversal in Slack/PagerDuty UI links.
SLO burn rate escalation rules are parameterizable per-customer and allow opt-in for aggressive shedding on dedicated/private contracts.
Security review completed and KMS-backed signing for runbook execution tokens in place (security_review_required = true).
implementation_notes: Signal scoring model: combine z-scored metric deltas (5m/1m), error-budget-burn-rate, and per-region capacity headroom into a 0-100 priority score. Weighting tuned via historical incident replay (see linked notebook).
Causal fingerprinting: hash top N contributing trace ids + metric signature + recent config change events to form group id. Use 5-minute sliding window to aggregate occurrences.

Dynamic thresholds: use percentile-based baselines per region and per route; threshold = baseline + k * stddev, where k is a function of desired false positive rate and current error budget; k computed by policy engine.

Runbook orchestrator: implement as idempotent state machine that records steps in Console event stream. Steps: 1) Inject low-impact mitigation (request-shed hint to load balancer), 2) Reduce best-effort batching to lower throughput, 3) Flip regional circuit (fallback to other region). Each step has reversible compensating action.

Safety checks: dry-run execution in sandbox region, automatic rollback on post-action health degradation (increase in error rate or latency > 10% vs pre-action), escalation to on-call after N failed automatic retries.

Integrations: PagerDuty (incident creation + ack-binding), Slack (context card with 'Runbook: Execute / Dry Run / Revert' buttons), Console (detailed diff + audit log), Telemetry (Grafana dashboard panel + synthetic canary hooks).
Metrics and dashboards: new SLO burn rate panel, dedupe-group incidence heatmap, runbook action success rate and mean time to mitigation (MTTM).
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring and fingerprinting logic with recorded historical incident traces.
End-to-end simulated failover tests in staging: 1) simulated regional latency spike 2) verify dedupe groups and single page creation 3) dry-run orchestrator in sandbox region.
Chaos test: induce cascading queue saturation in staging to validate staged mitigations and rollback criteria.
Load test: synthetic traffic to verify alert suppression rules do not hide true SLO violations at 3x normal traffic.
Runbook replay: run recorded playbook against historical incidents and compare operator actions vs orchestrator decisions (expected >= 80% overlap).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (week 1): deploy scoring & dedupe read-only mode in staging; create dashboards and alerts for scoring anomalies.
Phase 1 (week 2): enable dedupe & scoring in staging with synthetic incidents and runbook dry-run only; collect metrics.
Phase 2 (week 3-4): enable automated low-impact mitigations in a single non-critical region (blue) behind feature flag; on-call notified but not required to confirm.
Phase 3 (week 5): enable full orchestrator with human confirmation gate for aggressive steps; run limited rollout to small subset of customers and Dedicated pools.
Phase 4 (week 6-8): monitor, tune weights, expand to all regions; full enablement contingent on meeting reduction and fidelity acceptance criteria.
Rollback: feature flags per mitigation stage and global kill switch in Console; immediate rollback policy triggers on health checks failing for >5 minutes.
